reason: The cited evidence does not directly address the NbZrTiHfMo system or the specific mechanism linking Mo content to electronegativity difference and plasticity. E1 discusses Mo effects in Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloys, E2 and E3 cover Al effects in different RHEAs, and E4 discusses B2 ordering, none of which support the key premises about Mo reduction improving plasticity in this alloy.
premises: High Mo content increases electronegativity difference and lattice distortion in NbZrTiHfMo
Reducing Mo content will decrease electronegativity difference and lattice distortion
Reduced lattice distortion enhances dislocation mobility and room-temperature plasticity
Increasing Hf or Ti compensates for strength loss from Mo reduction via solid-solution strengthening
A 50% improvement in plasticity can be achieved while maintaining ~1700 MPa yield strength
